title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (1Mo-2Y nominal, $4B cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35) — the row reads verbatim announce 11/4/2026, operation 11/5/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 11/6/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 1Mo to 2Y, maturity range 12/06/2026 - 11/05/2028, min $0, max $4 billion. Stays estimate on the two counts every sibling in this family documents: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 11-04 operation announcement rather than this document, checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-buyback-7y10y-2026-09-17 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), reading the same schedule PDF that event verifies its own row against. It is the last row of the August-refunding schedule and the only one that was untracked anywhere in this calendar; every other row is already a tracked event or a sibling lane's proposal. WHY IT IS WORTH TRACKING RATHER THAN JUST NOTED: it is the exact opposite pole of the proposer's finding, at an identical cap, which makes it the cleanest available control. Primary data (fiscaldata buybacks_operations, 219 rows, fetched direct 2026-09-08): at a $4 billion cap this front-end bucket has filled the cap in 10 of 10 operations since 2024-05, on offer books of $16.5-69.0 billion — 9x to 17x cover — while the 7Y-10Y bucket at the SAME $4 billion cap has filled it 0 times in 9, on offers of $3.1-10.4 billion and a mean acceptance of $414 million. Same instrument, same cap, same acceptance rule, a factor of eight in what actually gets bought. That contrast is the evidence behind the proposer's correction that cap parity is not purchase parity, and this operation is where it can be re-measured. TWO CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER RESEARCHES IT. First, it lands the DAY AFTER the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding, which is both the expiry date of sb0607's doubled long-end sizing window and the meeting at which Treasury said further sizing would be addressed — so its own announcement will be read through a refunding that may have already changed the program, and the tentative row may not survive it. Second, the cap is not always $4 billion in this bucket: 2026-03-02 ran a $30 million cap, which is a rounding error rather than an operation, so a lower announced maximum is a live outcome and not an anomaly. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
